topIssues.title: Generate genesis with the op-deployer CLI instead of interopgen
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
The monorepo is removing `op-chain-ops/interopgen` and the in-process Go forge-script engine `op-chain-ops/script` as part of the op-geth decoupling ([optimism#21743](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21743), epic [optimism#20257](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20257)). op-deployer will run all deploy and genesis scripts through upstream forge instead. supersim's `just generate-genesis` builds its world with both packages, so it stops working at the first monorepo bump past that deletion. That bump also breaks supersim for a second reason: it imports `github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/superchain` ([`genesis/deployment.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/supersim/blob/4b12b035c67cc400cf7b95f2b8d88c9d072a4483/genesis/deployment.go#L9), [`config/chain.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/supersim/blob/4b12b035c67cc400cf7b95f2b8d88c9d072a4483/config/chain.go#L19)), which exists only in op-geth.

Until supersim bumps the monorepo, nothing breaks: the generator compiles against the pinned `contracts/lib/optimism` submodule.

## Proposal: generate genesis with the op-deployer CLI

Everything supersim needs from genesis generation is available in the op-deployer CLI today, at the current pin, except an L1 genesis output (see below). Once supersim drives the CLI, op-deployer switching to forge internally needs no further changes here.

1. **Commit an op-deployer intent** (e.g. `genesis/intent.toml`) replacing [`defaultRecipe`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/supersim/blob/4b12b035c67cc400cf7b95f2b8d88c9d072a4483/genesis/worldgen/worldgen.go#L18-L28):
   - custom intent, L1 chain 900, L2s 901–905, roles and `superchainRoles` from the dev mnemonic, `file://` artifact locators;
   - `useInterop = true` plus `globalDeployOverrides.devFeatureBitmap` with the `OptimismPortalInteropFlag` bit (op-deployer enforces that the two agree);
   - all `l2Genesis*TimeOffset` overrides set to `0x0`, including Lagoon;
   - `fundDevAccounts = true`. Extra prefunds go in `l1DevGenesisParams` / `l2DevGenesisParams` if still needed; anvil funds its own accounts.
2. **Rewrite `just generate-genesis`:**
   1. build the monorepo contracts and supersim's contracts (both recipes exist);
   2. run op-deployer built from the submodule (`go run` inside `contracts/lib/optimism`, so it matches the contracts): `init`, then `apply --deployment-target genesis`;
   3. per chain, `inspect genesis <id>` (the same `core.Genesis` JSON anvil's `--init` gets today) and `inspect l1 <id>`;
   4. write `900-l1-genesis.json` from the L1 state (see the op-deployer gap below);
   5. per L2, add supersim's own contracts offline with forge (next section).
3. **Delete** `genesis/worldgen/*` and `genesis/cmd/main.go`, which drops the `interopgen`, `script`, `opcm` and `foundry` imports. Also delete `DeployL2ValueTransferInteropContracts.s.sol`: with `useInterop`, `L2Genesis.s.sol` already sets up `SuperchainETHBridge` and `ETHLiquidity`.
4. **Addresses:** `inspect l1` returns `addresses.L1Contracts` with different field names (`OpChainProxyAdminImpl`, `L1Erc721BridgeProxy`, …). Convert it in [`genesis/deployment.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/supersim/blob/4b12b035c67cc400cf7b95f2b8d88c9d072a4483/genesis/deployment.go#L101-L113), e.g. with `genesis.CreateL1DeploymentsFromContracts`. This also fixes an existing bug: `ProxyAdmin` resolves to zero today because the generated addresses JSON names it `OpChainProxyAdmin`. A naive unmarshal leaves `AddressManager` zero and fails `TestL1GenesisState`.

### supersim's own L2 contracts

The periphery scripts (Promise, `L2NativeSuperchainERC20`, `GasTank`, Uniswap v4) rely on `vm.etch`, `vm.store` and `vm.deal`, which forge does not broadcast, so running them against a live anvil does not work. Run them offline on top of the op-deployer L2 allocs instead. The hooks already exist from supersim's earlier forge pipeline: `runWithStateDump(allocsPath, outputPath)` in [`DeployL2PeripheryContracts.s.sol`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/supersim/blob/4b12b035c67cc400cf7b95f2b8d88c9d072a4483/contracts/script/DeployL2PeripheryContracts.s.sol#L29) and `CombineAllocs.s.sol`.

Per chain: extract `.alloc` from the `inspect genesis` output, run `forge script … --sig 'runWithStateDump(string,string)' --chain-id <id>`, and write the dump back into `.alloc`.

- `--chain-id` is required: `PositionManager`'s EIP-712 domain caches `block.chainid` as an immutable.
- `DeployL2AuxiliaryContracts.s.sol` needs a `runWithStateDump` too, or one wrapper script runs all of them.
- Diff the old and new allocs once at the fixed addresses to confirm what `vm.dumpState` leaves out (the sender and the script contract).

### Diff risk

- **Unchanged:** predeploys, Promise, `0x420beef…01/02` and the Uniswap CREATE2 addresses hardcoded in [`interop/applier.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/supersim/blob/4b12b035c67cc400cf7b95f2b8d88c9d072a4483/interop/applier.go#L28-L38). Those depend only on supersim's own contract build.
- **Changed:** every L1 address. Code reads them from the embedded addresses JSON. The docs hardcode some, and those are already stale: `docs/src/guides/deposit-transactions.md` and `docs/src/getting-started/first-steps.md`.
- **Tests:** CI has no regeneration drift check. The anvil end-to-end tests cover genesis (`TestL1GenesisState`, `TestGenesisState`, `TestAccountBalances`, the deposit tests, and the fork-mode `TestForked*` tests that exercise `applier.go`). Optionally add a unit test asserting code at the `applier.go`, Promise and `0x420beef…` addresses in the embedded genesis.

## What op-deployer needs in the monorepo

Tracked under [optimism#21743](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21743):

- **L1 genesis CLI output.** The genesis-target L1 header lives in `State.L1DevGenesis`, which is `json:"-"` ([`state/state.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/cd4fddebd79cae68d7b18cf0eeaca54a6992f075/op-deployer/pkg/deployer/state/state.go#L75)). Only `l1StateDump` (base64 + gzip allocs) is persisted, and `inspect` has no L1 genesis subcommand. The header timestamp is taken at seal time, so it can't be rebuilt afterwards. Needed: persist the header and add an `inspect l1-genesis`. Until then, supersim can decode it with `jq -r .l1StateDump | base64 -d | gunzip` and wrap it in a minimal header, since anvil overrides the timestamp and chain ID anyway.
- **Parity of the forge-based genesis target** with what supersim relies on: `useInterop` together with the matching `devFeatureBitmap`, `fundDevAccounts`, dev prefunds, fork-offset overrides, L1 preinstalls, deterministic L1 addresses in genesis mode (zero CREATE2 salt), and the `inspect genesis` / `inspect l1` output shapes.
- **Optional:** a hook to add extra L2 genesis allocs inside op-deployer. supersim doesn't need it because it doesn't use the rollup config; merging allocs outside op-deployer changes the L2 genesis hash.

## Sequencing

This can land at the current pin, independent of the monorepo work. The current generator keeps working only for the pinned contracts, because its Go bindings must match the Solidity script inputs. The migration therefore has to land before supersim's next monorepo bump past the `interopgen` deletion.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*
